item.description: Large crowds gathered at Dam Square in Amsterdam on Sunday, for a pro-Palestinian demonstration marking three years since the start of Israel’s war on Gaza, Anadolu reports. Demonstrators carried Palestinian flags and called for an end to violence against Palestinians. Participants also urged the international community to take action and impose sanctions on Israel. Since October 2023, Israel’s war in Gaza has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and injured over 175,000, according to Palestinian figures. item.title: The president who can’t say his name
item.description: Three weeks before Michigan decides whether to send the first Muslim senator to Washington, the president still cannot or will not say the man’s name. “Mike Rogers, the great American Patriot and Republican Candidate for the U.S. Senate from Michigan, completely obliterated Mohammed El-Sayed in the big debate tonight,” Trump wrote on Truth Social after Thursday’s debate. Rogers had skipped it. “Mohammed is a Jihadist lunatic who hates our Country, the Black People of Detroit, and wants to see the U.S. fail.” The candidate’s name is Abdul El-Sayed. Mohamed is his middle name, inherited from his Egyptian immigrant father. He rarely uses it. Yet the president repeats it so relentlessly that it reads less like a mistake than a strategy […]

item.title: Indonesian, Egyptian presidents condemn Israeli settlement expansion in Jakarta talks
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and his Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah el-Sisi condemned Israel’s illegal settlement expansion during bilateral talks in Jakarta on Sunday, according to Indonesia’s state-run Antara news agency. “We strongly condemn Israel’s illegal settlement construction and actions that only worsen the situation,” Subianto said in a joint statement, calling for an immediate de-escalation of regional conflicts, Antara reported. The two leaders expressed concern over violations of international law and military operations causing civilian casualties, reaffirming their support for a two-state solution. Subianto pledged continued humanitarian aid and diplomatic support for Palestinians, warning that further escalation threatened global stability. item.title: Iran’s security chief calls US response to deal conditions ‘inadequate’
item.description:
Iran’s security chief calls US response to deal conditions ‘inadequate’

Washington must clarify its position before talks on a possible agreement can advance, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei says.

“The Americans have now responded to us. In their response, they have accepted some of our conditions, while others remain unclear,” the Supreme National Security Council secretary told the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

Rezaei described the US response as “inadequate”.

“We are no longer in the process of responding to the Americans,” he said. “They must clarify the issues that remain unclear to us,” he added.

The exchange follows President Donald Trump’s rejection late last month of an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.

US Vice President JD Vance subsequently demanded a “meaningful” reduction in Iran’s uranium enrichment capacity as a condition for an agreement.

Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman
item.description:
Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman

Mohsen Rezaei has accused the Trump administration of recruiting “thugs” to smuggle oil through coastal waters off Oman.

Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary said the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command also participate in the operation, according to state-linked news agency ISNA.

Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Rezaei said.

He said the operation relies on a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers”, adding that Iran attacks them “every night”.

Seventy-two killed in air strike on gold mine near Sudan-Egypt border
item.description:
Seventy-two killed in air strike on gold mine near Sudan-Egypt border

Sudanese rights group The Emergency Lawyers on Sunday accused Egypt's air force of an air strike which killed 72 workers at a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border a day earlier.

"The attack carried out by Egyptian military aircraft", on Saturday, "resulted in the deaths of 72 civilian miners, according to preliminary information, while efforts to document and verify the casualty toll are ongoing", the rights group said.

item.title: Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz
item.description:
Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz

Iran’s security chief claimed on Sunday that US President Donald Trump's adminitation hired “thugs” in the coastal waters of Oman to smuggle oil through the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei was quoted as saying by Iran's ISNA news agency.

Rezaei said that the smuggling operation involves the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command (Centcom) using a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers” and that Iran targets them “every night”.
